notes: The task brief for this workstream suggested a 1987-1988 upgrade window; the only dated upgrade sourced in this session is the CERN archives guide's 'Between 1985 and 1987, the UA2 detector was upgraded' (src:ua2-cern-archives-guide). That sourced range (1985-1987) is used instead of inventing 1987-1988.

home.cern's narrative ('UA2, which saw its first collisions in December 1981') and INSPIRE's date_started (1981-11) differ by about a month; INSPIRE (rank 3, day/month-precision field) is used as the sourced start, with the home.cern quote recorded here for completeness.

physics_goals.quote: The main aims are a study of the W and Z bosons and a search for the top quark.
physics_goals.value: Study the W and Z bosons and search for the top quark using complete electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry

physics_goals.quote: Other topics include the production of direct photons at high p(t), establishing new bounds on leptoquark masses, and a search for the charged Higgs from the top decay.
physics_goals.value: Measure direct-photon production at high transverse momentum, set bounds on leptoquark masses, and search for a charged Higgs boson from top-quark decay

summary.plain: A particle detector built around CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron in the early 1980s, alongside UA1, when the machine was turned into a proton-antiproton collider. UA2 co-discovered the W and Z bosons using precise calorimeters rather than a magnetic spectrometer.
summary.technical: Collider detector at the CERN SppS, operated 1981-1990, built around complete electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry down to about 5 degrees to the beam, without a muon system; upgraded in 1985-1987 with a scintillating-fibre tracker and later a silicon detector. Co-discovered the W (Jan 1983) and Z (1983) bosons with UA1 and searched for the top quark.

unique_capabilities.quote: The apparatus has complete calorimetry, both electromagnetic and hadronic, down to about 5 degrees to the beams. Electron identification is achieved by means of calorimetry, preshower, and transition radiation detectors.
unique_capabilities.value: Complete electromagnetic and hadronic calorimetry down to about 5 degrees from the beam, with no muon detector, relying on calorimetry, preshower counters and transition-radiation detectors for electron identification
